issue.title: Update: Django_Security_Cheat_Sheet
issue.body:
## What is missing or needs to be updated?
The [Django_Security_Cheat_Sheet.md](https://github.com/OWASP/CheatSheetSeries/blob/master/cheatsheets/Django_Security_Cheat_Sheet.md) currently lacks a consolidated, secure-by-default `settings.py` configuration example that shows how to enforce production security settings by default while overriding them safely in a local `.env` environment. It also misses practical settings like `__Host-` cookie prefixes, `SECURE_CROSS_ORIGIN_OPENER_POLICY`, `SECURE_REFERRER_POLICY`, and a complete `SECURE_CSP` (Django 6.0+) dictionary example.

## How should this be resolved?
Add an **Application security configuration** section before the Admin panel URL section containing:
- A fail-safe `settings.py` snippet using `django-environ` and `django.utils.csp` where HTTPS redirects, HSTS, security headers, `__Host-` cookies, and CSP are enabled by default.
- A corresponding `.env` snippet showing which parameters to override for local development without HTTPS.

I have already prepared and submitted the implementation in PR #2970.

issue.title: Django Security: secure defaults, __Host- cookies, Referrer-Policy and COOP

2970.title: Django Security: secure defaults, __Host- cookies, Referrer-Policy and COOP
2970.body:
Adds short, sourced guidance to existing sections of the Django Security Cheat Sheet: production values as the defaults, with required values read from the environment without a fallback (General Recommendations), `__Host-` cookie names (Cookies), and keeping Django's `same-origin` Referrer-Policy and COOP defaults (Headers).

Please make sure that for your contribution:

- [ ] In case of a new Cheat Sheet, you have used the [Cheat Sheet template](../templates/New_CheatSheet.md).
- [x] All the markdown files do not raise any validation policy violation, see the [policy](https://github.com/OWASP/CheatSheetSeries/actions?query=workflow%3A%22Markdown+Link+Check%22).
- [x] All the markdown files follow these [format rules](../CONTRIBUTING.md#markdown).
- [ ] All your assets are stored in the **assets** folder.
- [ ] All the images used are in the **PNG** format.
- [x] Any references to websites have been formatted as `[TEXT](URL)`
- [x] You verified/tested the effectiveness of your contribution (e.g., the defensive code proposed is really an effective remediation? Please verify it works!).
- [ ] The CI build of your PR pass, see the build status [here](https://github.com/OWASP/CheatSheetSeries/actions).

## Scope and sourcing (required)

- [x] This PR is focused: it modifies a single cheat sheet, or a small coordinated set, and the scope is described in the PR body.
- [x] Every technical claim, recommendation, or threat assertion added in this PR is supported by a primary source (RFC, NIST, OWASP standard, vendor documentation, peer-reviewed research) linked inline as `[text](URL)`.
- [x] I have read each source I cite and confirm it actually supports the claim. I have not relied on summaries, hearsay, or model-generated citations.

This PR fixes issue #2971.

## AI Tool Usage Disclosure (required for all PRs)

Please select exactly one of the following options. PRs that leave this section blank will be closed.

- [ ] I have NOT used any AI tool to generate the contents of this PR.
- [x] I have used AI tools to generate the contents of this PR. I have verified
    the contents and I affirm the results. The LLM used is `Gemini Argon`
    and the prompt used is `Reviewed my existing production settings.py snippet for fail-safe defaults; prose written manually`. I have independently verified every citation and technical claim against the cited source. Rework after review: the LLM used is `Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)` and the prompt used is `Read PR #2970 and the review comment, and fix what the review asks to change.` Claude checked the diff against the repository's review checklist, rewrote the bullets and checked them against the Django 5.2 and 6.1 docs. I reviewed the result and read every cited source myself.
